record.original_question: Let A and B be the generators of two communicating C0 -semigroups on a Banach space and let G be the generator of the corresponding product semigroup. Find (the most general) conditions implying D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).

evidence.quote: Problem (Generator of product semigroups). Let A and B be the generators of two communicating C0 -semigroups on a Banach space and let G be the generator of the corresponding product semigroup. Find (the most general) conditions implying D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space, and let $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ and $(S(t))_{t\ge 0}$ be two strongly continuous one-parameter semigroups of bounded linear operators on $X$ (i.e., $C_0$-semigroups), with infinitesimal generators $A$ and $B$, defined on their domains $D(A), D(B) \subset X$ respectively. Assume the two semigroups commute, that is, $T(t)S(s) = S(s)T(t)$ for all $t,s \ge 0$. Define the product family $U(t) := T(t)S(t)$ for $t \ge 0$. Then $(U(t))_{t\ge 0}$ is again a $C_0$-semigroup on $X$; let $G$ denote its infinitesimal generator with domain $D(G)$. It is known that $G$ is the closure of $A+B$ on $D(A)\cap D(B)$, but in general $D(G)$ may be strictly larger than $D(A)\cap D(B)$.

Problem: Determine the most general conditions on $A$ and $B$ (or on the semigroups $T$ and $S$) which guarantee the equality
$$D(G) \;=\; D(A) \cap D(B).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Standard semigroup theory (e.g., Trotter-type results) establishes that for two commuting $C_0$-semigroups the product is a $C_0$-semigroup whose generator is the closure of $A+B$, but a fully general characterization of when $D(G)=D(A)\cap D(B)$ is not available; only sufficient conditions (e.g., one generator bounded, both analytic with suitable sectoriality, or Kato/Da Prato–Grisvard type maximal regularity hypotheses) are known. Web search did not locate a definitive result settling the most general such condition, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the product of class A semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: A product semigroup S(t) = T_t T'_t is also a semigroup of class A, whose generator is the closure of A + A'.
status_evidence.claim: The generator of the product of commuting semigroups is the closure of A+B, but equality of domains is not in general established.
